This has been a pain point for several users. I would encourage you try the upcoming release 1.3 where vectorized parsers are available. You need to go to github, select the 1.3 branch and hit the download button and install from the tar gz file, but it's a lot faster for csv when using vectorization (add the option vectorized = T). You should get the same data frame in output.


Antonio

Dear Antonio Piccolboni

Thank you very much for your advice. We have installed version 1.3 of rmr and we have done some tests with the 'vectorized = T' option of from.dfs(). However, when we try to read a 300 MB .csv file (containing 35 million lines), the problem is the same: it takes long time to execute and give no answer (no error message, no cursor return). We also noticed that this task uses 100% of only one core and it is not parallelized at all. Is that normal or we are missing something?

The input data comes from a table in Hive. We exported this table in .csv format and try to read it in RHadoop as explained above. Is there a connector to read data from Hive directly into RHadoop ?

As function from.dfs() give no log message, we decided to use function mapreduce() as follows:

smac = mapreduce(
    '/tmp/data.csv',
    input.format = make.input.format('csv', sep=','),
    structured = T,
    map = function(k, v) keyval(k%%3500, v),
    reduce = function(k,vv) keyval(k, vv)
)   

In this execution, the reduce phase takes too much time and fails with the following message: Task attempt_201208031318_0277_r_000051_0 failed to report status for 600 seconds. Killing!
Is there a way to overcome this problem?
Thank you very much in advance.

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#238] Re: Trying to read a 300 MB .csv file
parts:
Hi,
 the fact that you talk about from.dfs and send an example without any call to from.dfs is certainly not helpful. The parallelism level depends on your hadoop configuration, at least for the map phase, so you may want to test it with some java code, like the built in examples, to be sure you can leverage your cluster in full and take rmr out of the equation for a moment. Your data set is not that big so it is likely that hadoop doesn't think worth it to unleash more than one process at it. See below an example of reading 1M records in 2 seconds, that is not what hadoop was invented for. from.dfs doesn't aim for parallelism, its role is to load into main memory the results of a computation when they are of a reasonable size (small GBs) so that's not the point. The call that triggers mapreduce jobs which should be parallel is mapreduce, but there you don't specify the vectorized option so it's reading a line at a time  which should be about 1K times slower than vectorized =T. It's a problem with the csv parser, you won't see this kind of speed ups using vectorized in other contexts, but it really is mandatory when reading csvs. This is for 1M records

> system.time({from.dfs("../RHadoop.data/airline.1000000", vectorized=T, format = make.input.format("csv", sep = ",", header = T))})
2012-08-10 09:22:12.435 java[58105:1903] Unable to load realm info from SCDynamicStore
2012-08-10 09:22:12.479 java[58105:1903] Unable to load realm info from SCDynamicStore
2012-08-10 09:22:13.280 java[58119:1903] Unable to load realm info from SCDynamicStore
2012-08-10 09:22:13.331 java[58119:1903] Unable to load realm info from SCDynamicStore
12/08/10 09:22:13 WARN util.NativeCodeLoader: Unable to load native-hadoop library for your platform... using builtin-java classes where applicable
   user  system elapsed 
  3.096   0.618   2.353 

on a meager mac laptop. Keep also in mind that if you specify the format wrong read.table can take forever, just forgetting the headers can be a big deal. Try to read.table(.. ) in the first 1M records and see how it works. from.dfs calls read.table behind the curtains for the csv format.
Finally, there is one thing that you need to do to be able to handle big data. You need to start on small data sets (in local mode) and then build up to the real thing. We have a nifty debugging guide document up on the wiki in need of some company. At each level, new bugs and problems pop up and they get harder to troubleshoot, so you are much better off making sure that your code works for 10, 100, 1000 etc records before you unleash it on 35M, it doesn't work, game over. It's not only rmr that needs to be developed for like that, this is a generally accepted reality of developing for big data that I just learned from others  and from experience and pass it on to rmr users.


Antonio

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#238] Re: Trying to read a 300 MB .csv file
parts:
smac = mapreduce(
    '/tmp/data.csv',
    input.format = make.input.format('csv', sep=','),
    structured = T,
    map = function(k, v) keyval(k%%3500, v),
    reduce = function(k,vv) keyval(k, vv)
)

Actually I am seeing something else. If you read a csv, csv has no notion of a key, so all the data goes into v as a data frame with vectorized = T and structured =T and k is NULL if I remember right. So that k%%3500 is probably returning numeric(0) which means there is only one reducer and one single reduce call, which means the list vv (which gets coerced to a data frame because of the structured option), which means you must be running out of memory as well. My guess is v$some.column.name%%3500 is needed there or similar, You may want to simply skip the reducer and try a map only job, be sure that it does what you think it should and then add the reducer back in.


Antonio
